primary_sources: Google Machine Learning Production Best Practices

rules.rule_name: Strict Data Leakage Prevention and Splitting
rules.explanation: Applying pre-processing transformations (e.g., scaling, normalization, imputation) on the entire dataset before splitting causes data leakage from the test set into training.
rules.do: Split data into train/validation/test sets BEFORE fitting scalers, encoders, or imputation transformers.
rules.dont: Do not compute global dataset statistics (mean, std, vocabulary) across test splits during data pre-processing.

rules.explanation: Manual, ad-hoc feature transformations make ML experiments non-reproducible and prone to production execution errors.
rules.do: Encapsulate feature engineering inside reproducible pipelines (e.g., Scikit-Learn Pipeline, ColumnTransformer, or PyTorch Dataset classes).
rules.dont: Do not rely on loose, unscripted Jupyter Notebook cell transformations for training pipeline data preparation.

rules.explanation: Complex deep learning architectures should always be benchmarked against simple, interpretable baseline models to justify added computational complexity.
rules.do: Establish simple baselines (e.g., Logistic Regression, Dummy Classifier, basic heuristic) before testing complex ensembles or neural networks.
rules.dont: Do not deploy high-complexity deep learning models without comparing performance and latency against simple baselines.

rules.explanation: Standard accuracy metrics fail on imbalanced datasets, causing models to predict only majority classes.
rules.do: Apply domain-appropriate techniques (SMOTE, class weighting, focal loss, stratified sampling) for skewed class distributions.
rules.dont: Do not evaluate imbalanced classification tasks using standard accuracy alone.
